input.question: How can airbnb inflate rental and housing prices; shouldn't competition drive down prices?
input.ground_truth: AirBnB drives down ***short term rental*** prices. AKA "hotel" prices. It does this at the expense of decreasing the housing supply and ***driving up*** prices for long-term accommodations like homes and condos. In a simple supply and demand equation, it increases the supply of SHORT TERM accommodation (like hotel rooms) - reducing their cost- and decreases the supply of long-term accommodations (like houses) - increasing their cost.

messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How can airbnb inflate rental and housing prices; shouldn't competition drive down prices?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let's imagine you and your friend both sell lemonade on your block. Normally, if both of you are selling lemonade, you might try to make your lemonade sound extra special or maybe lower the price a little so more people will buy from you, right? That's how competition usually works—when lots of people are selling the same thing, they try to make it cheaper or better for you.

But now, let's say Airbnb comes into town and tells some people that they can rent out their extra room or their whole house to visitors. Lots of people start putting their rooms or houses on Airbnb. At first, you might think, "Yay! There are so many places to stay, maybe the prices will be low!"

But here’s the tricky part: sometimes, when there are lots of places to stay, the people who want to visit (like tourists) don't have many other choices. So, if everyone is using Airbnb, and there aren't as many regular hotels, the people who want a place to stay might have to pay more because there aren't that many other options left. Also, if the city makes it hard to build new hotels, and only allows a few places to be turned into short-term rentals, then there are fewer places to stay than people who want them. This can make the prices go up instead of down.

Also, some landlords see that they can make more money by renting out their apartments on Airbnb for a few days at a high price, instead of renting them out to someone for a whole month at a lower price. So, they take their apartments off the long-term rental market, which means there are fewer places for people to live, and the prices for regular apartments can go up too.

So even though there are lots of places to stay listed on Airbnb, sometimes there aren't enough for everyone who wants one, or the rules make it so there can't be enough. That's why prices can go up instead of down, even when there seems to be a lot of competition.
